evidenceSummary.excerpt: There was another young hunter who encountered Diana and her maidens in the woods, but he met with a kinder fate at the hands of the goddess than did poor Actæon, whose only fault had been a most natural curiosity.
The fleet-footed Diana was no more ardent in the chase than was the hunter Orion, who roamed the forest all day with his faithful dog, Sirius.
Orion continued to hunt from early dawn until nightfall without any misfortune overtaking him on account of his impetuous love-making.
When Apollo learned of his sister's affection for the young hunter, he was very angry, for Diana had refused the love of the gods, and had begged of Jupiter the right to live unwed.
Diana mourned Orion[15] many days; and to keep his memory honored she placed him and his faithful dog, Sirius, in the sky as constellations.
